Scope: Source-ready OpenSSH Server capability installation candidate for unattended setup
UserDecision: Make OpenSSH Server available as a selected unattended-install option. Keep capability installation separate from starting sshd and enabling inbound firewall access. Preserve pre-existing service, firewall, configuration and host-key state.

MicrosoftReference.RelevantBehavior: Installing OpenSSH Server creates and enables the OpenSSH-Server-In-TCP inbound TCP/22 firewall rule. Service startup is a separately documented action.

Behavior: Requires an already elevated native process and explicit computer/build/edition identity.
Refuses servicing while reboot is pending and refuses ambiguous provider state.
Uses ShouldProcess before saving state or invoking servicing.
Installs only the Server capability and never starts sshd.
Restores a TCP/22 allow rule to disabled when it was absent or disabled before servicing.
Preserves a pre-existing enabled TCP/22 rule and reports that exposure remains.
Passes an explicit local source and LimitAccess when requested.
Saves a protected pre-install observation before servicing; exact capability removal/recovery is not implemented.
Writes a completed post-install snapshot with capability, service, firewall and server-data observations.
Removes the capability only when a matching saved run began with no service, firewall rule or server data and those surfaces have not drifted.
If capability removal leaves the exact disabled TCP/22 rule created by the saved run, removes that rule and verifies absence.
Writes an idempotent removal record after verifying NotPresent capability and absence of service, firewall rule and server data.
